content: As a software developer maintaining the GitHub repository pulp-platform_axi_pr185, you are responsible for analyzing a submitted issue and identifying the exact location in the repository where the issue occurs.

Here is the issue description:
# axi_dw_up/downsizer: Latch inference when synthesizing with Mentor Precision
When synthesizing with _Mentor Precision_, the tool infers latches in the `axi_dw_upsizer` and `axi_dw_downsizer`.
Seems the tool has an issue with the automatic variable `r_data` and `w_data` in both modules.
Links to the of the offending codelines of `axi_dw_upsizer` and `axi_dw_downsizer`:
https://github.com/pulp-platform/axi/blob/f847575bab7269f88f6caa36f01275de2007378a/src/axi_dw_upsizer.sv#L478-L492
https://github.com/pulp-platform/axi/blob/f847575bab7269f88f6caa36f01275de2007378a/src/axi_dw_upsizer.sv#L595-L607
https://github.com/pulp-platform/axi/blob/f847575bab7269f88f6caa36f01275de2007378a/src/axi_dw_downsizer.sv#L550-L562
https://github.com/pulp-platform/axi/blob/f847575bab7269f88f6caa36f01275de2007378a/src/axi_dw_downsizer.sv#L722-L737
At least in `axi_dw_upsizer` the assignment of `r_data` should still be the default `'0`. So `r_data` is only _saving_ the initialization value, which is then conditionally overwritten.
Then however when synthesizing with _SYNOPSYS_ the latches are not there.
When adding an `else` statement to the `if` then the latch goes away at least in the first code snippet. So an idea for a fix from my side is to add the `else` condition and remove the automatic variable.

Your task is to:
1. Carefully review the issue description and thoroughly analyze the issue to uncover all possible causes.
2. Review the provided code file and identify at least three locations within the file that require inspection or modification to resolve the issue.

Guidelines for Specifying Locations:
1. The locations can be specified as class names, function or method names, or exact line numbers.
2. Line ranges may span across multiple classes or methods if necessary. Ensure all line numbers are accurate and within the valid range of the provided code.

IMPORTANT:
1. Analyze how the provided code file relates to the issue and identify at least three related locations that require modification (e.g., edits, additions) or require inspection (e.g., provide important context).
2. If a new method or class needs to be added to resolve the issue, specify a broader line range that includes surrounding code to provide context and ensure proper placement.
3. Check if any dependencies, helper methods, or global variables should be modified to ensure logical and structural coherence.
4. Check the functionally similar or similarly named methods/classes that might have the same bug or require consistency updates.

<analysis>
The latch inference is caused by conditional assignments to the packed data fields inside two always_comb blocks in axi_dw_downsizer: one in the read‐path (where r_data is declared as an automatic variable) and one in the write‐path (where w_data is an automatic variable). Mentor Precision sees that r_data and w_data only get assigned under certain conditions and infers latches for the bits that aren’t explicitly assigned in the “else” paths. The two key regions are inside the gen_read_downsizer block (around the mst_resp.r_valid condition) and inside the write‐path block (around the slv_req_i.w_valid condition). To fix this, each of these conditional blocks needs a matching else to drive the data fields to a known default (for instance all zeros), or r_data/w_data can be removed in favor of an explicit default assignment to r_req_d.r.data and mst_req.w.data. 
Three locations requiring inspection or modification:
1. The entire gen_read_downsizer always_comb block, so you can see how r_req_d is initialized and where r_data is used.
2. The specific lines where automatic slv_data_t r_data is declared and used under if (mst_resp.r_valid).
3. The write‐path always_comb block where automatic mst_data_t w_data is declared under if (slv_req_i.w_valid).
</analysis>
